atoms.text: Captain Sally has just arrived at Pirate Island. Can you help her find the treasure?

trainers.instruction: Captain Sally wants a map that can help her to read the coordinates of the treasure chest. Which map should she use?

hint.text: Remember, the map should be on squared paper, the numbers should be spaced evenly and on the lines and the axes should be correctly labelled.
hint.sound: Remember, the map should be on squared paper, the numbers should be spaced evenly and on the lines, and the axes should be correctly labelled.

wrong1.text: It can’t be this map because the x-axis and y-axis are the wrong way round.

wrong2.text: It can’t be this map because it is not on squared paper.

wrong3.text: It can’t be this map because the numbers are not evenly spaced or written on the lines.

atoms.text: She arrives at the first location and sees something shiny behind the anchor. Select it to pick it up.
It looks like part of a key!

instruction.text: What are the coordinates of the base of the palm tree?

hint.text: Remember, we always go along the corridor first and then up the stairs.

atoms.text: She arrives at the next location and sees something gold in the sand by the trunk of the tree. Select it to pick it up.
It’s the second part of the key!

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to complete the coordinates of the barrel.

atoms.text: She arrives at the barrel and sees something on top of it. Select it to pick it up.
It’s the final part of the key!

instruction.text: Looking at the map, the treasure chest covers two positions. Write the coordinates in the gaps to label both of them.

atoms.b: The coordinates of the treasure chest are (6, <mat><gap>7</gap></mat>) and (<mat><gap>7</gap></mat>, 7).

atoms.text: Captain Sally pulls out the key and tries it in the lock. Select the chest to open it.
It’s open and Captain Sally is rich beyond her wildest dreams! Thanks for helping!
atoms.sound: It’s open, and Captain Sally is rich beyond her wildest dreams! Thanks for helping!
